FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Registration needs injury and property coverage first, with injury benefits paying your own hurt regardless of fault and property benefits paying damage you cause others [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Owners prove coverage at registration, carry at least $10,000 of each kind from a Florida-licensed carrier, keep it continuous, and keep proof in the car [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Cars present 90 days in the last 365 must stay insured, carriers report lapses to the state, failures suspend for up to three years, and plates go back before policies cancel [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A02
Stopped drivers without proof must prove coverage in court or face suspension, and convicted lapses reinstate between $150 and $500 [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A02
Suspensions past 30 days allow plate seizure and jail time up to a year with a $1,000 fine, bar temporary licenses, punish fake cards as misdemeanors, and grant hearings on request [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A02
Crash drivers prove financial responsibility by insurance or state certificate, and DUI convicts carry $100,000, $300,000, and $50,000 tiers for three years [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A02
Point, crash, habitual-offender, and serious-offense cases carry $10,000, $20,000, and $10,000 tiers or $30,000 combined, with lapses suspending up to three years and at-fault damages prepaid [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A03
Learner minors drive daylight only until three months pass, then to 10 pm, while sixteen-year-olds stop from 11 pm to 6 am and seventeen-year-olds from 1 am to 5 am, all excused for work or a 21-plus companion [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A03
License crimes span altering, misusing, lending, fraudulent applications, dual credentials, unlicensed loans and rentals, and false statements to officers, courts, or crash reports [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A03
Disabled permits waive meter fees and open reserved spaces while transporting the owner, and borrowed permits draw misdemeanor charges, $500 or six months, plus towing and confiscation [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A03
DUI covers driving or controlling a car under alcohol, controlled, prescription, or store-bought drugs, suspends at arrest for BAL .08 or refusal, and compels blood, urine, or breath tests by implied consent [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A04
Test refusal suspends one year automatically, a second refusal stretches 18 months with a misdemeanor, and fatal or injurious crashes force a professional blood draw even unconscious [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A04
A first DUI draws $500 to $1,000, 50 service hours, a year of probation, six months jailed, 180 revoked days, 12 school hours, an addiction check, and possible interlock, all harsher with high BAL or a young rider [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A04
A second DUI draws $1,000 to $2,000, nine months jailed, 180 revoked days, 21 school hours, an addiction check, and a year of interlock, doubled in fines when enhanced [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A04
A third DUI draws $2,000 to $5,000, twelve months jailed, 180 revoked days, 21 school hours, an addiction check, and two interlock years [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A04
Under-21 drivers lose six months at BAL .02, take a substance course at .05, trigger parent notice under 19, and lose the license for any drug conviction [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A05
Cars hauling, selling, or abetting drug felonies may be seized and forfeited as contraband [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A05
Roadway litter up to 15 pounds costs $100, while heavier dumps bring misdemeanor charges, $1,000, three points, and cleanup duty [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A05
Bus passing draws a citation, school, four points, and $265 or $465, while injurious passing adds 120 service hours, a panel, six points, a year out, and $1,500 [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A05
Rim driving damages roads unlawfully, belts must cross hips and chest rather than hiding behind backs since airbags never substitute, and child seats must fit child, car, and caregiver with under-13 riders behind [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A06
Rear-facing seats never face airbags, hired-ride restraints fall on parents, belts bind drivers, front riders, and under-18 passengers, under-4 riders need seats with 4-and-5 riders seated or boosted, drivers answer for minors while adults answer for themselves, and fitting help runs free [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A06
Belt exemptions cover certified medical cases, paper carriers, old school buses, paid buses, farm gear, trucks past 26,000 pounds, and favor or emergency rides for ages 4 and 5 [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A06
Every motorist must know and obey limits, Florida caps them at 70 mph, and speeding tickets cost fines and points [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A07
Exceeding limits past 50 MPH costs $1,000 then $2,500, and school or work-zone speeding doubles fines toward $1,000 with a possible course [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A07
Charged crash drivers face court on officer-filed counts, and at-fault injury crashes or second collisions in two years force a collision-avoidance course [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A07
A third crash offense inside 36 months forces a 12-hour advanced course, four wheel hours, and an extended test, lapsing to cancellation past 90 days [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A07
Point totals suspend 30 days at 12 in a year, three months at 18 in 18 months, and a year at 24 in 36 months, counting out-of-state convictions equally [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A07
Minors reaching 6 points in a year drop to business-only driving for a year, extended 90 days per further point [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A08
Speeding draws 3 points to 15 over, 4 past 16, and 6 in a crash, scene-leaving over $50 draws 6, and texting draws 3 plus 3 in school zones or 6 in a crash [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A08
Signals, bus passing, and reckless driving each draw 4 points, injurious bus passing draws 6, and restricted-hour driving plus handheld use in protected zones draw 3 [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A08
Suspension starts with fraudulent applications, unlawful license use, court orders, and intoxication-test refusals [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A09
Suspension continues through restricted-license misuse, point totals, unpaid fines and no-shows, support lapses, missing insurance, bus failures, retail theft, and dropouts [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A09
Revocation ends privileges for intoxicated driving, vehicle felonies, deadly hit-and-runs, ownership lies, triple recklessness, vehicle immorality, major or point-count histories, drug felonies, failed vision, and racing [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A09
Cancellation voids licenses issued wrongly, won by false papers, or tied to unfinished schooling [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A09
Hardship and reinstatement run through review offices, DUI alcohol and refusal appeals need hearings inside 10 days of arrest, and first offenders may trade review rights for a restricted license there [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0039]
